question: Has anyone ever numerically computed an eigenvalue of the Dirac (spinor) operator on a hyperbolic 3-manifold (cusped or closed, any spin structure, any method)?
verdict_qualified: No numerically computed NONZERO Dirac eigenvalue on any hyperbolic 3-manifold was found. A near-miss exists that constrains the wording: Lin-Lipnowski certify ZERO eigenvalues (spectral-flow crossings) of spin^c Dirac operators on CLOSED hyperbolic 3-manifolds by computer-assisted means, without computing any eigenvalue value.

conditions: The qualifier 'nonzero' MUST be present (Lin-Lipnowski pin the eigenvalue zero).
The qualifier 'cusped' is recommended (their manifolds are closed).
Lin-Lipnowski arXiv:2506.07238 MUST be cited as nearest prior work, with the distinction stated.
The MathSciNet gap (§depth) must be carried in the caveat.
safe_phrasings: first computed nonzero Dirac eigenvalue value on a hyperbolic 3-manifold
first numerical Dirac spectrum on a cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold
forbidden_phrasings: first Dirac eigenvalue on a hyperbolic 3-manifold (unqualified)
first computation of Dirac spectral data on a hyperbolic 3-manifold
first_gate_ruling.note: B940's seal already EXCLUDES the kernel (lambda=0, dim 2). The prior art lands on exactly that excluded object. Alignment is fortunate but must be stated explicitly, not relied on silently.

nearest_prior_art.citation: Francesco Lin, Michael Lipnowski, 'Dirac spectral flow and Floer theory of hyperbolic three-manifolds', arXiv:2506.07238 (2025)
nearest_prior_art.operator: 1-parameter family of spin^c Dirac operators D_{B_tau} associated to flat spin^c connections
nearest_prior_art.what_is_computed: certified localization of spectral-flow zero-crossings; e.g. s_0(tau)=0 for some tau in [0.1537, 0.1556] for the unique self-conjugate spin^c structure on census #357; second crossing tau in [0.4467, ...]
nearest_prior_art.method: odd Selberg trace formula and its derivative; complex length spectrum via SnapPy to cutoff R in [7, 8.5]; Dirichlet-domain geodesic triangulations of 150-200 tetrahedra; hours to ten days CPU per example
nearest_prior_art.numbers_published: parameter values (tau), volumes, systoles, H_1 torsion, C_Y norm bounds
nearest_prior_art.eigenvalue_values_published: NONE (the only eigenvalue pinned is exactly zero)
why_not_prior_art_for_B940: all published numbers are parameters tau, not eigenvalues
the only eigenvalue determined is 0, which B940's seal excludes
their manifolds are closed; m004 is cusped (different spectral regime under Baer's dichotomy)
their own 'first' claim is for monopole Floer chain complexes, not Dirac eigenvalues

control.meaning: The surface literature DOES contain numerically computed spinor eigenvalues, so the 3-manifold null is a real result and not a search artifact.
control.citation: E. Gesteau, S. Pal, D. Simmons-Duffin, Y. Xu, 'Bounds on spectral gaps of hyperbolic spin surfaces', arXiv:2311.13330 (2023), publ. 2025
control.method: Selberg trace formula with geodesic length spectrum as input (their section 4); numerical STF method credited to Lin-Lipnowski JAMS 2022; plus SDP/bootstrap for the bounds
control.convention: lambda_1^(1/2) := 1/4 + t_1^2, where |t_1| is the lowest nonzero positive Dirac eigenvalue

computed_values.note: values tabulated in their Appendix B

contrast_computed_dirac_spectra_on_non_h.note: Explicit Dirac spectra on 3-manifolds exist only where closed forms exist (flat and spherical), never hyperbolic. This is the expected pattern and it sharpens the null.
citations: F. Pfaeffle, 'The Dirac spectrum of Bieberbach manifolds' (2000) - flat
S. Boldt, 'Properties of the Dirac spectrum on three dimensional lens spaces' (2017) - spherical
C. Baer, 'The Dirac operator on space forms of positive curvature' (1996) - Killing spinors

depth.mathscinet_failure_mode: HTTP 302 redirect to subscription authentication wall

depth.tool_note: This session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before the task began; the sweep was executed over raw HTTP against bibliographic APIs instead, which yielded verbatim records, full-text search and citation-graph traversal rather than summarized keyword hits.

methods_used.name: citation-graph traversal (highest yield)
methods_used.detail: Enumerated and read the COMPLETE citing set of Baer 2000: cites:W2130197549 -> 56 works, cites:W2951147165 -> 3 works. Every one is theoretical; no numerical eigenvalue computation of any kind.

methods_used.name: zbMATH MSC-structured sweep
methods_used.detail: 20 queries across cc:58J50, cc:53C27, cc:57M50, cc:11F72, cc:65N25 plus phrase queries; ZERO_RESULTS semantics verified against a nonsense-query control.

methods_used.name: reverse direction
methods_used.detail: Identified everyone who numerically computes ANY spectrum on hyperbolic 3-manifolds (Inoue, Grunewald-Huntebrinker, Bonifacio-Mazac-Pal) and checked each for spinor crossover. All scalar or integer-spin.

methods_used.name: author-level crossover check
methods_used.detail: Inoue, Then, Aurich, Grunewald, Strohmaier checked for Dirac/spinor publications. None produced a hyperbolic Dirac numerical spectrum.

methods_used.name: full-text reading of decisive papers
methods_used.detail: arXiv:2506.07238 (~185k chars via HTML extraction) and arXiv:2311.13330 (~214k chars via pdftotext) read and grepped for numerics, tables, eigenvalue statements.

methods_used.name: adjacent-literature sweep
methods_used.detail: eta invariants/spectral flow; analytic torsion/Ruelle zeta; quantum chaos spinor billiards; lattice/discretized Dirac; hyperbolic band theory; SnapPy/Regina/Snap tooling.

key_negatives_verified: Baer 2000 computes accumulation RATES under degeneration and proves the discrete-vs-R dichotomy; no numerical eigenvalue. (Also the source of m004's authorization: dimension 3 with one cusp forces a non-trivial spin structure, hence discrete spectrum.)
Pfaeffle 2003/2004 is a convergence theorem (spec M_i -> spec M with multiplicity) via spinorial escaping sets; no numbers.
Park 2001/2005 eta invariants are trace-formula-analytic; no numerics. This closes the 'eta invariants sometimes need eigenvalues' lead.
Monk-Stan 2023/2024 is spectral DENSITY convergence for random Weil-Petersson surfaces; asymptotic, 2D, no individual eigenvalues.
Bolte-Stiepan 2006 is a trace formula for compact hyperbolic SURFACES; theory, no computed spectra. No 3-manifold sequel exists.
Martelli-Reid 2022/2025 classifies cusp spin structures (bounding vs Lie) and applies Baer's dichotomy; no eigenvalues.
Bonifacio-Mazac-Pal arXiv:2308.11174 covers hyperbolic 3-manifolds but only functions and powers of the cotangent bundle: integer spin, no Dirac.
SnapPy/Snap/Regina have no spinor or Dirac spectral capability; they supply length spectra only.
Camporesi-Pedon compute Dirac eigenfunctions on hyperbolic SPACE H^n (symmetric space, continuous spectrum), not on a finite-volume quotient.
residual_risk: MathSciNet not consulted; its review corpus overlaps zbMATH heavily but is not identical.

A number buried in a paper body or appendix whose title/abstract/review never mentions it would be missed by metadata search. Partly mitigated: OpenAlex default search is a full-text index and was used.

English-language and modern-era bias; older print proceedings and non-indexed lecture notes are thin. Partly mitigated: zbMATH indexes German/French dissertations and returned Pfaeffle's Hamburg thesis.
Paywalled full text could not be searched systematically.
A hyperbolic-3-space fermionic eigenmode could hide in older quantum-cosmology literature under different vocabulary; INSPIRE queries returned nothing but the vocabulary space is large.
recommendation: Bank OUTCOME A with the word 'first' PERMITTED but only in a phrasing carrying the qualifier 'nonzero' (and preferably 'cusped'), citing Lin-Lipnowski arXiv:2506.07238 positively as nearest prior work and stating the distinction. Carry the MathSciNet gap in the depth caveat verbatim. Citing the near-miss is stronger science than an unqualified priority claim.
